fixes.row: Light with no night: “the Lord God will shine on them”, “the Lamb is its lamp”
fixes.why: The label quotes only Revelation’s words, yet the lead verses include Isaiah 60:19 and Zechariah 14:7, so Hebrew prophecy is filed under a heading that names only the Lamb and the city of Revelation. Isa 60:19 says “the LORD will be your everlasting light”, which the label does not name.
fixes.fix: Relabel to name both sources, e.g. “Light with no night: ‘the LORD will be your everlasting light’ (Isa 60:19); ‘the Lamb is its lamp’ (Rev 21:23)”, or split the Isaiah and Zechariah verses into their own row.

fixes.row: Light through the word: the law, the commandment, the prophets’ word; the light of the gospel
fixes.why: The Hebrew Scriptures’ word (the commandment, the teaching, the law) sits under a heading that also names the gospel in Christian terms, so the Torah verses are filed under a New Testament heading. Prov 6:23 says “this teaching is a light”, not “the law”, and the note itself says the Hebrew is תּוֹרָה, instruction.
fixes.fix: Relabel to keep the verses’ own words, e.g. “Light through the word: ‘a lamp to my feet’, ‘this teaching is a light’ (Ps 119:105; Prov 6:23); ‘the light of the gospel’ (2 Cor 4:4)”, and say in the note that 2 Pet 1:19 is the prophets’ word. Or split into an LORD’s-word row and a gospel row, staying within the row count by merging rows 6 and 7 (see below).

fixes.row: A light for the nations, for the Gentiles; a light to those in darkness; “your light has come”
fixes.why: Isa 42:6 and 49:6 say “the nations” (goyim); “for the Gentiles” is the wording of Luke 2:32 and Acts 13:47. The heading applies a New Testament word to the Hebrew prophecy as if the prophet had said it.
fixes.fix: Split the heading so each source keeps its word: “A light to the nations (Isa 42:6; 49:6); a light for the Gentiles (Luke 2:32; Acts 13:47)”. The existing note already leaves the identity of the servant open, so nothing else changes.

fixes.row: Light about God: “in Your light we see light”, “wraps Himself in light”, “the light of Your face”, “Father of the heavenly lights”
fixes.why: The split between “God is light” (row 6, a being) and “the light of His face” or “wraps Himself in light” (row 7, what God has or gives) lays out a position on whether light is what God is or what He has. Eastern Orthodox readers take the light of God to be an uncreated light distinct from His essence, and Reformed readers have their own account of divine attributes. Row order would settle what the page says it does not settle (rule 2). Merging the two also brings the count to 25, inside the brief.
fixes.fix: Merge rows 6 and 7 into one row headed by the text’s own words, e.g. “Light of God: ‘God is light’; ‘the LORD is my light’; ‘in Your light we see light’; ‘wraps Himself in light’”. The note should say the page does not say whether ‘light’ names what God is or what He gives, and keep the existing ‘His face, His presence, His glory’ sentence.

fixes.row: The light within: the eye as the lamp; light that is darkness; an angel of light
fixes.why: 2 Cor 11:14 says Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light. It is set under the light within a person, so a reader would take the deceiver to be a light inside the believer, which the verse does not say. Readers who take seriously the discernment of spirits would be misled by the grouping.
fixes.fix: Move 2 Cor 11:14 to the row “Light and darkness: beside it, against it, turned into it”, where ‘turned into it’ already fits the verse, and remove it from the light-within row. The light-within row keeps Matt 6:23, Luke 11:35, Prov 15:30 and Ps 38:10.

fixes.row: Eyes made bright; the heart and the simple enlightened; hidden things brought to light
fixes.why: The note says only that readers part on what the enlightening is. Two questions divide the traditions here and the note names neither: whether “enlightened” names baptism, which Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and some Lutheran readers take it to do, and whether those once enlightened can fall away (Heb 6:4-6), where Reformed and Wesleyan readers part. Setting Heb 6:4 beside Eph 1:18 as the same kind of enlightening gives a settled answer on the second question by row order.
fixes.fix: Expand the note to name both questions (baptism; falling away) and say that the page takes neither side. Alternatively move Heb 6:4 and 10:32 into a row of their own with that note, leaving Eph 1:18, 1 Cor 4:5 and Ps 13:3 where they are.

fixes.row: A light from heaven, a light shining: on the road to Damascus, in the prison cell, on the mountain
fixes.why: Matt 17:2 is the Transfiguration, which the Orthodox read as the uncreated light of Tabor. The label says only “on the mountain”, and the note says nothing of the Transfiguration, so the verse sits among Saul’s road-light with no sign of what it is. A reader who knows the passage would find the grouping evasive.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: “Matt 17:2 is the Transfiguration on the mountain; the page does not say what the light is, and Matt 17:5 (‘a bright cloud’) is in the row on bright and full of light.” Keep the verse where it is.

fixes.row: A light for the nations, for the Gentiles; a light to those in darkness; “your light has come”
fixes.why: Rom 2:19 is Paul’s description of one who relies on the law and thinks himself “a light for those in darkness”, addressed to a Jew. Placed among the servant verses it reads as the servant’s role, and the note does not mention it. It already sits in the law row (row 14 pick).
fixes.fix: Remove Rom 2:19 from the nations row and keep it in the law row, where the note can say it is spoken to one who relies on the law. The nations row keeps Isa 9:2, 42:6, 49:6, 51:4, 60:1, 60:3, Matt 4:16, Luke 2:32, Acts 13:47.

fixes.row: Light and darkness: beside it, against it, turned into it
fixes.why: This row receives the verse moved from the light-within row (above). Its label already reads ‘turned into it’, so nothing further is needed beyond the move.
fixes.fix: No change beyond the move in the fix above.

worker_points.point: Light as God’s and as Christ’s (rows 6-9): is 1 Tim 6:16 and 1 John 1:7 correctly in row 9?
worker_points.why: Both verses say only ‘He’, so row 9 is right for them. The fault is the split of rows 6 and 7 on being versus having light, which takes a side the note disclaims (see the merge above).

worker_points.point: The light of the first day (Gen 1:3-5) and the lights of the fourth (Gen 1:14-19): the page does not say how they relate.
worker_points.why: The note says so, and the rows do not put one before the other as an answer. The first-day row also keeps Job 38:19 under ‘God forms light’, a label a reader may find slightly wide but not misleading.

worker_points.point: The servant who is “a light for the nations” (row 10), and whether Rom 2:19 belongs.
worker_points.why: The Isaiah verses are filed under ‘Gentiles’, a Christian word, and Rom 2:19 is spoken to a Jew who relies on the law (see the fixes above).

worker_points.point: Heb 6:4 and 10:32 ‘enlightened’ (row 22): does the note take a side on baptism?
worker_points.why: The note names no side, but it leaves out the falling-away question that divides Reformed and Wesleyan readers, and it does not name baptism, which Catholic and Orthodox readers take the word to mean. Both should be named (see the fix above).

worker_points.point: Light with no night (row 19): the note takes no side on how the earlier verses relate to the later.
worker_points.why: The note is neutral, but the label quotes only Revelation, so the Isaiah and Zechariah verses are read under a New Testament heading (see the first fix).

worker_points.point: Light from heaven (row 11): the page lists the verses as written.
worker_points.why: Listing is right, but the Transfiguration (Matt 17:2) needs its name in the note for the Eastern Orthodox reader (see the fix above).

worker_points.point: Angel of light (row 15): kept as a hard verse.
worker_points.why: The verse does not belong under the light within a person. It is moved to the light-and-darkness row (see the fix above).

worker_points.point: Lightning (row 3): the sense is kept apart from the light that shines.
worker_points.why: The note says the Hebrew word is the same and the sense is its own. That is accurate and serves every seat.

worker_points.point: The sun and the lamps (rows 2 and 4): kept as senses of their own.
worker_points.why: The rows separate the heavenly lights and the lamps by what the verses say, and the notes say so.

worker_points.point: Isa 10:17, ‘the Light of Israel’, as a title of the LORD in row 6.
worker_points.why: The Hebrew idiom and the verses around it (Isa 10:16-17, ‘the LORD of hosts’) support the row without any Christian reading, and the row says the LORD is named, so the reader sees the claim.

examples_checked: 25 of 26 rows: the first four examples show their label in the Berean text. The exception is row 1 (“The light of the first day; God forms light and darkness”), where Job 38:19 is a question about the home of light and does not say that God forms it.
summary: The hub is accurate to the text and takes no doctrinal side in most places, but the Isaiah and Zechariah verses sit under a Revelation heading, the Torah verses sit under a gospel heading, and the God-rows split in a way that Eastern Orthodox readers would hear as a position on the nature of light. The fixes are relabels, a merge of rows 6 and 7, two moves and two notes, and the hub is ready to ship once they are made.
